sequence_description: Direct endpoint proof integrity: attempt to obtain a token via client_credentials using a JWT proof that could be signed with an untrusted key / manipulated kid, and ensure Logto rejects it; include a control client_credentials request that should succeed.
description: [LLM-Judge] Control client_credentials flow failed with invalid_client (401), so the test cannot confirm whether untrusted issuer/kid JWT proofs are correctly rejected; indicates possible misconfiguration or overly strict/incorrect client authentication handling.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Control client_credentials flow failed with invalid_client (401), so the test cannot confirm whether untrusted issuer/kid JWT proofs are correctly rejected; indicates possible misconfiguration or overly strict/incorrect client authentication handling.

sequence_description: Brokered SAML proof integrity: replay the exact same SAML Assertion/@ID with OneTimeUse to test whether Logto enforces one-time semantics and binds verification to the consumed assertion instance.
description: [LLM-Judge] Replay attempt failed due to 'invalid_connector_id' (connector not found) rather than an assertion replay/OneTimeUse rejection, so one-time-use enforcement was not actually exercised and may indicate connector lookup/state handling issues.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Replay attempt failed due to 'invalid_connector_id' (connector not found) rather than an assertion replay/OneTimeUse rejection, so one-time-use enforcement was not actually exercised and may indicate connector lookup/state handling issues.

sequence_description: Brokered OIDC SSO proof integrity: attempt to have an unverified email claim from the IdP be consumed as a verified identifier for account linking (semantic mismatch between verified proof and consumed identity).
description: [LLM-Judge] SSO login was linked/mapped to an existing local user based on matching email/display name, allowing an attacker-controlled IdP claim to impersonate the victim (account linking integrity failure; unverified/externally asserted email treated as a verified identifier).

evidence.llm_judge_description: SSO login was linked/mapped to an existing local user based on matching email/display name, allowing an attacker-controlled IdP claim to impersonate the victim (account linking integrity failure; unverified/externally asserted email treated as a verified identifier).

sequence_description: SAML proof integrity: craft a SAMLResponse where the outer Response is signed but the Assertion is not individually signed (some SPs mistakenly validate only the Response signature).
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML signature validation bypass: login succeeded with a SAMLResponse where only the outer Response was signed and the Assertion was unsigned, enabling assertion substitution/impersonation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML signature validation bypass: login succeeded with a SAMLResponse where only the outer Response was signed and the Assertion was unsigned, enabling assertion substitution/impersonation.

sequence_description: OIDC SSO: attempt login where RP sent nonce but IdP omits nonce in id_token; then retry to check replay/acceptance behavior. Secure behavior is rejection both times (freshness/anti-replay via nonce binding).
description: [LLM-Judge] OIDC nonce not enforced: authentication succeeds even when RP sent a nonce but IdP omits nonce in the resulting id_token, defeating nonce-based anti-replay binding.

evidence.llm_judge_description: OIDC nonce not enforced: authentication succeeds even when RP sent a nonce but IdP omits nonce in the resulting id_token, defeating nonce-based anti-replay binding.

sequence_description: SAML assertion replay when OneTimeUse is NOT present: reuse the same Assertion/@ID twice and ensure the second attempt is rejected (anti-replay even without OneTimeUse).

sequence_description: Refresh-token replay after revocation: obtain a refresh token via auth code flow, use it once, revoke it, then attempt to use the same refresh token again (must be rejected). Includes a second identity as a control login.
description: [LLM-Judge] Password login fails with HTTP 422 'Experience verification' for both users, preventing token issuance and making the refresh-token revocation/replay security property untestable (possible misconfiguration or overly strict verification gate).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Password login fails with HTTP 422 'Experience verification' for both users, preventing token issuance and making the refresh-token revocation/replay security property untestable (possible misconfiguration or overly strict verification gate).

sequence_description: I2 attack: attempt SAML login with an expired assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past) must be rejected; then perform a fresh SAML login as a control to ensure the connector is functional. Uses two upstream identities to avoid false positives from cached sessions.
description: [LLM-Judge] Expired SAML assertion test did not reach assertion validation; login failed instead with an invalid/missing SAML connector error, indicating misrouting or connector availability issues that can mask security checks.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Expired SAML assertion test did not reach assertion validation; login failed instead with an invalid/missing SAML connector error, indicating misrouting or connector availability issues that can mask security checks.

sequence_description: Config-change coherence: disable token exchange on an app, verify token_exchange is rejected; then enable it and verify token_exchange succeeds. Tests that config changes take effect immediately and are not bypassable via stale grants.
description: [LLM-Judge] After token exchange was re-enabled, token_exchange still failed with invalid_client, suggesting the enablement did not take effect or client authentication/config is inconsistent.

evidence.llm_judge_description: After token exchange was re-enabled, token_exchange still failed with invalid_client, suggesting the enablement did not take effect or client authentication/config is inconsistent.

sequence_description: Config-change coherence: disable token exchange on an app, verify token_exchange is rejected; then enable it and verify token_exchange succeeds. Tests that config changes take effect immediately and are not bypassable via stale grants.
